summary.text: Dan Kessler is the Democratic candidate for the Minnesota State Senate, District 48, in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against incumbent Julia Coleman (R).
In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as a psychologist, small business owner and longtime Chaska resident.

paragraphs.text: Dan Kessler said in a Ballotpedia survey that he has been a practicing psychologist for 30 years, including 15 years in a primary care clinic as well as work in hospital, community mental health and private practice settings, before starting his own business.
He said he is a public school parent and that Carver County has been his home for two decades.
Kessler was the Democratic nominee for Minnesota House District 47B in 2020, when he lost to incumbent Greg Boe (R), 48.3 percent to 51.5 percent.
In 2022 he won the Democratic primary for Minnesota State Senate District 48 and lost the general election to incumbent Julia Coleman (R), 45.6 percent to 54.3 percent.
In the 2026 survey, Kessler listed affordability, holding people who commit fraud accountable, and public safety including gun violence as campaign messages.
He said he wants to make health care and prescription drugs more affordable, citing his own health experience, and that he would vote for any good anti-fraud bill regardless of its sponsor's party.
